text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 15 in history.
70 BC - Virgil (or Vergil) born as Publius Vergilius Maro, and considered the greatest Roman poet. He wrote "The Aeneid", an epic 12-book tale of the founding of Rome by Aeneas of Troy.

1542 - Akbar (Abu-ul-Fath Jalal ud-din Akbar) born. One of the greatest emperors of India. He conquered the rebellious states of Gujarat and Kashmir as well as Afghanistan. He was a great reformer and abolished slavery.
1581 - Commissioned by Catherine De Medici, the "Ballet Comique de la Reine" was staged in Paris. A spectacle of dancing, this is often considered to be the first major ballet.
1582 - In Italy and Spain, this day became the first day of the Gregorian Calendar after it was adopted by Pope Gregory XIII. Ten days would be eliminated thus October 5 1582 became October 15.
1608 - Evangelista Torricelli born. Italian physicist and mathematician, he discovered the principle of the barometer.
1815 - Desposed French emperor Napoleon Bonaparte landed on the Island of St Helena, where he had been sent into exile by the British after his defeat at the Battle of Waterloo.

1844 - Friedrich Nietzsche born. German philosopher and poet who repudiated Christianity, liberal ethics and democratic ideals. His views were said to have been a great influence on the formation of the Nazi movement.
1878 - Paul Reynaud, French statesman born. As prime minister in 1940, he failed to prevent France's occupation by the Germans, and was imprisoned for the duration of World War Two.
1880 - Marie Stopes born in Edinburgh. Early advocate of birth control, she founded Britain's first clinic for contraception in 1921.
1881 - P.G. (Pelham Grenville) Wodehouse born. British author and humourist who created the characters of Bertie Wooster and his valet Jeeves.
1900 - Mervyn Leroy born. U.S. film director whose films included "Little Caesar", which launched a whole gangster cycle. He also directed "Gold Diggers of 1933" and "Random Harvest".
1917 - Arthur Meier Schlesinger born. U.S. historian and writer. He won a Pulitzer Prize in 1946 for "The Age of Jackson", and later became a speechwriter for John F. Kennedy.
1917 - World War One's most famous spy, Mata Hari, was executed by firing squad at Vincennes Barracks, outside Paris.
1928 - The German airship Graf Zeppelin completed its journey across the Atlantic from Friedrichshafen to Lakehurst, New Jersey.
1945 - Pierre Laval was executed for betraying his country during World War Two. As premier of Vichy France (1942-1944), he pursued a policy of collaboration with Nazi Germany.
1946 - Hermann Goering, Nazi leader and one of Hitler's most loyal supporters, committed suicide in his prison cell just before he was due to be executed.
1959 - Sarah Ferguson born. Known as "Fergie" she became Britain's Duchess of York when she married Prince Andrew in 1986. They are now divorced.
1964 - Nikita Khrushchev was deposed as First Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party, and replaced by Leonid Brezhnev with Alexei Kosygin becoming prime minister.

1964 - Cole Porter, U.S. composer and lyricist, died. He wrote over 20 Broadway musicals including "Kiss Me Kate", and songs such as "Let's Do It", "Begin the Beguine" and "Anything Goes" which became worldwide hits.
1970 - Australia's West Gate Bridge, being built over Melbourne's Yarra River, collapsed killing 34 workmen.
1978 - Electoral college confirms General Joao Baptista Figueiredo as Brazil's new president.
1990 - Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev won the Nobel Prize for Peace.

1990 - Former KGB double agent Oleg Gordievsky named John Cairncross as the alleged "fifth man" in a group of British agents who rocked British intelligence in the 1950s and 1960s after being unmasked as Soviet moles.
1994 - President Jean-Bertrand Aristide stepped back on to Haitian soil to a joyous welcome, ending three years of exile that began when he was deposed in 1991.
1995 - Millions of Iraqis voted "Yes" for Saddam Hussein as president in a referendum. Foreign observers in Iraq as guests of the government said the referendum seemed free and fair to them.
